subtopicTitle: Least squares — normal equations, QR approach

cards.front: State the normal equations for the linear least-squares problem min ||Ax - b||_2.
cards.back: A^TAx = A^Tb, where A is m×n with m ≥ n.

cards.front: Derive the normal equations by setting the gradient of ||Ax-b||_2^2 to zero.
Give the closed-form solution of the normal equations when A has full column rank.
For A = QR (thin QR, Q^TQ=I), state the least-squares solution x.
Derive why x = R^{-1}Q^Tb solves the least-squares problem.
cards.back: Substitute A=QR into normal eq: (QR)^T(QR)x = (QR)^Tb ⇒ R^TRx = R^TQ^Tb. Multiply by (R^T)^{-1}: Rx = Q^Tb ⇒ x = R^{-1}Q^Tb.

cards.front: Why is the QR approach numerically preferable to forming and solving the normal equations?
cards.back: A^TA squares the condition number (κ(A^TA)=κ(A)^2) and loses information; QR works directly with orthogonal Q, preserving conditioning.

cards.front: What matrix must be invertible for the thin-QR least-squares solution to be unique?
cards.back: R (the upper-triangular factor) must be nonsingular, equivalent to A having full column rank.
